The sum can be written as  

\[
S=\sum_{k=0}^{9}\sin\!\left(\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{24}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{24}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)
   =\frac12\sum_{k=0}^{9}\Bigl[\cos\frac{\pi}{6}-\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{2(2k+1)\pi}{24}+\frac{\pi}{6}\Bigr)\Bigr].
\]

Since \(\cos\frac{\pi}{6}= \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\),  

\[
S=\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}-\frac12\sum_{k=0}^{9}\cos\!\left(\frac{(2k+3)\pi}{12}\right).
\]

The cosine terms are for angles  

\[
\frac{3\pi}{12},\frac{5\pi}{12},\dots,\frac{21\pi}{12},
\]

whose sum equals  

\[
\sum_{k=0}^{9}\cos\!\left(\frac{(2k+3)\pi}{12}\right)=
-\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{2}.
\]

Hence  

\[
S=\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}
   =\frac{10\sqrt3+\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.
\]

None of the three proposed answers (\(\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}\), \(\frac{1+\sqrt3}{4}\), \(\frac{11\sqrt3+2}{4}\)) matches this exact value.

**Final choice:**  

CHOICE: NONE
